title: Effort vs. Efficiency: How Ideal‐Self Pursuit Shapes Consumer Preference for Substitutional AI ‐Powered Products
abstract: ABSTRACT As artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly takes over human tasks, a critical question arises regarding the trade‐off between effort and efficiency in consumer decision‐making: despite AI's remarkable sophistication and its ability to enhance efficiency, why do many consumers still prefer to perform certain tasks themselves rather than delegate them to AI? Prior research has primarily examined this phenomenon from the perspectives of perceived competence and trust, while relatively little attention has been paid to the role of self‐identity, particularly ideal‐self pursuit. Integrating identity‐based motivation theory and self‐discrepancy theory, this study examines how ideal‐self pursuit shapes consumer responses to substitutional AI‐powered products in domains where personal effort and capability development are central to attaining the ideal self. Across a field study and four experiments, we find that consumers with stronger ideal‐self pursuit exhibit lower preference and reduced willingness to pay for substitutional AI‐powered products. Perceived self‐threat moderates this effect, and the moderated relationship is mediated by consumers' self‐improvement motivation. Specifically, under high (vs. low) perceived self‐threat, ideal‐self pursuers show an even lower preference for AI‐powered products that replace effort aimed at self‐improvement. Importantly, this effect should not be interpreted as a wholesale rejection of AI. When AI‐powered products are positioned as tools that support rather than substitute consumers' self‐improvement efforts, ideal‐self pursuit can instead increase consumer preference. These findings offer a novel perspective on consumer responses to AI‐powered products and provide implications for positioning AI technologies in ways that better align with consumers' identity‐related motivations.

title: Low-Power End-to-End Cochlear Implant Speech Denoising with Spiking Neural Networks
abstract: Cochlear implants (CI) restore hearing for individuals with severe to profound hearing loss. However, CI users often struggle to understand speech in noisy environments. Deep neural networks (DNN) have shown promise in enhancing speech for CI users, yet their high energy demands make them non-ideal for low-power CI processors. Spiking neural networks (SNN), on the other hand, offer comparable performance with significantly lower energy consumption. Hence, we propose a novel SNN inspired by the Deep ACE architecture that simultaneously performs speech enhancement and CI coding. Our model achieves competitive vocoded short-time objective intelligibility (VSTOI) and signal-to-noise ratio improvement (SNRi) scores compared to Deep ACE, while achieving more than a sixfold reduction in energy consumption.

title: RASA: Disentangled Spatial-Motional Priors for Cross-Identity Character Animation
abstract: Cross-identity character animation aims to drive a target identity from a reference image to follow the motion of a source character from a driving video. The core challenge lies in the inherent entanglement of two capabilities: cross-identity spatial mapping (aligning position, scale, and skeletal proportions) and motion control (refining joint articulation, volumetric consistency, and view coherence). We introduce Reference-Aware Structural Alignment (RASA), a framework that disentangles spatial mapping from motion control by injecting structured priors into a Diffusion Transformer (DiT). Our approach has two stages. First, a Spatial Prior Calibrator (SPC) fuses reference identity with driving pose to generate a spatially grounded initial noise latent, ensuring correct positioning, scaling, and alignment with the driving skeleton. Second, an Inherent Motional Guider (IMG) encodes shape-agnostic SMPL articulation parameters into a semantic motion vector beyond appearance-biased 2D keypoints. Injected into intermediate DiT layers, this vector complements the base pose condition for anatomically consistent articulation and view-aware volumetric refinement. We curate CIM-Bench, a high-quality benchmark with rigorous curation, for evaluation. Extensive experiments show RASA significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in motion fidelity and visual quality. Our work establishes a new paradigm showing disentangled spatial and motional priors are key to robust character animation. Project page: https://hidream.ai.github.io/RASA/

title: Adaptive Diagonal Fisher Preconditioning: Escaping Vanishing Gradient Plateaus via Bounded Information Geometry
abstract: Standard Euclidean optimizers like SGD and Adam frequently experience catastrophic failure when models encounter overconfidence traps, causing probabilities to saturate and gradients to vanish on flat optimization plateaus. This vulnerability is especially pronounced in deep architectures utilizing saturating activation functions. In this work, we propose theAdaptive Lipschitz optimizer (AL) anchored to the Bernoulli variance bound and regularized by an exponentially decaying topological dampening shift. We prove that our update rule guarantees monotonic loss reduction under an L-Lipschitz smoothness assumption. To bridge theory and practice, our implementation strictly enforces the theoretical learning ratebounds derived in our proof. Empirical evaluations on both deep sigmoid MLPs and Mini-Transformers trained on WikiText-2 demonstrate that while standard methods suffer from rapid gradient norm collapse or volatile initialization spikes, our Adaptive Lipschitz metric acts as a mathematical shock absorber, preserving gradient health and scaling robustly to natural language processing tasks. *Author DisclaimerAll underlying concepts, frameworks, and core research directions are the original work of the author. Generative AI tools were used strictly for assistance in manuscript drafting, code generation, and figure preparation. All theoretical formulations and mathematical proofs included herein are unverified AI-generated drafts shared as preliminary proposals for discussion and community review.

title: A Microkernel Language Model: Design Principles and a Recurrent Binding Precursor
abstract: We ask whether an architecture-level authority structure can be made artifact-checkable and honestly graded. We propose a Microkernel Language Model research program with a nested conformance ladder (R → G0 → G1(ρ)) plus an orthogonal service-readiness flag (S), and report a recurrent binding precursor, not a Microkernel LM proper. The program target is G1(ρ)+S. The present artifact holds R only: before each of three weight-tied passes, a token-wise codebook assignment re-stamps a typed 64-dimensional residual slice at a stable telemetry and intervention point. Dense transformer paths also write that slice, the full residual crosses passes (ρ=1), and no service adapter is implemented. A scalar cross-iteration feedback edge is causally inert at inference in P1 and is reported as such. The 23.9M-parameter model trains from scratch within the BabyLM 2026 Strict-Small budget. One independent R2 run reproduces end-to-end trainability and scores 65.83 on BLiMP and 18.92 on revised entity tracking. Across four P1 seeds, forcing three-pass weights to one pass lowers BLiMP by 3.2–4.5 points; the paired gain over a 27M monolith is +0.9±1.0 and compute-confounded. A benchmark revision removes an earlier entity advantage and exposes a leaked completion prior. Functional privilege of the reserved slice remains unverified. The contribution is an operational, artifact-checkable taxonomy, a recurrent composition with reproduced end-to-end trainability, and an audit discipline that reports failed mechanism and capability claims rather than absorbing them into aggregate scores. Submitted to the BabyLM Challenge 2026 (Strict-Small track) as Submission 3; not accepted (decision 2026-08-28; the stated reason was submission volume, and no reviews were returned). Posted here as a preprint. The text is identical to the submitted version; the only changes are the author block, the removal of review line numbers, and a file-header comment.

title: Distributed Differential Privacy with Federated Learning via Lagrangian Relaxation
abstract: Achieving strong differential privacy guarantees within the constraints of federated learning, especially when utilizing complex models, remains a significant challenge. This work proposes a novel framework leveraging Lagrangian relaxation to address this issue. The core idea involves incorporating a Lagrangian term directly into the federated learning objective function to formally represent the differential privacy constraint. This allows for an iterative solution of the resulting Lagrangian problem via distributed optimization, providing a controllable mechanism for balancing privacy and model accuracy. The proposed approach offers a more practical and scalable solution compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios where precise control over the privacy-accuracy trade-off is desired. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual discussion, outlining a pathway for future research and implementation.

title: Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Performance in XTREME-R: Scaling Model Size and Intermediate Task Difficulty
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does the choice of intermediate task difficulty (e.g., simple vs. complex) impact zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance on XTREME-R when scaling model size from 125M to 1B parameters? title: Information Geometry and Deep Reinforcement Learning: A Unified Framework
abstract: This paper investigates a novel framework for reinforcement learning (RL) that integrates the principles of information geometry with deep neural networks. The core challenge in RL, particularly within high-dimensional state spaces, lies in effectively representing and navigating complex environments. Traditional RL methods often struggle with the curse of dimensionality, leading to slow learning and suboptimal policies. This work proposes a solution by leveraging information geometry to characterize the geometry of the state space. Specifically, we utilize Riemannian manifolds to represent the state space, allowing us to compute intrinsic geometric properties like geodesics and curvature. These geometric insights are then incorporated into the deep reinforcement learning process, primarily as a potential reward function. This approach aims to guide the learning of an optimal policy by exploiting the inherent structure of the state space, leading to improved sample efficiency and performance, especially in dynamic environments. We outline the key components of this framework, including the construction of the Riemannian manifold, the design of the potential reward function based on geometric information, and the integration with a deep neural network actor-critic architecture. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential future research directions and the overall impact of this unified framework on the field of RL. ---

title: Quantum-Inspired Noise Injection for Robust Feature Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-inspired noise injection techniques to enhance the robustness of feature learning algorithms. Traditional machine learning models are notoriously vulnerable to adversarial attacks and noisy data, leading to unpredictable and unreliable performance. We hypothesize that mimicking the effects of quantum decoherence – a fundamental phenomenon in quantum physics characterized by the loss of quantum information due to interaction with the environment – can provide a novel and effective strategy for improving model robustness. Our approach introduces carefully calibrated noise into the training process, specifically targeting the representation learning stage. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework, that this noise injection process forces the model to learn more resilient features, less susceptible to small perturbations and statistical variations. The core claim of this work is that precisely controlled, quantum-inspired noise injection can substantially elevate a model's resilience against adversarial attacks and noisy data. We outline a design strategy for this noise injection and discuss its potential impact on various feature learning algorithms.

title: Quantum Algorithms Based on Quantum State Superposition
abstract: This paper explores the design of parallel algorithms leveraging the principle of quantum state superposition. The core idea is to exploit the inherent parallelism within quantum systems to simultaneously process multiple problems, thereby enhancing computational efficiency. The proposed approach involves decomposing problems into multiple quantum states, utilizing quantum gates to induce superposition and interference, and ultimately arriving at solutions. This work presents a fundamental design methodology, focusing on the theoretical aspects of superposition-based parallel algorithms. The algorithm's effectiveness relies on the ability to manipulate quantum states with high fidelity and minimize decoherence. Further research is needed to explore the practical implementation of these algorithms on existing quantum computing platforms.

title: COMPUTER ENGINEERING AND CYBERSECURITY INTEGRATION IN CYBER-PHYSICAL & ROBOTIC SYSTEMS
abstract: This article comprehensive survey investigates the critical intersection of Computer Engineering and Cybersecurity within the domain of modern cyber-physical and robotic infrastructure. As embedded architectures migrate toward distributed edge-cloud computing paradigms, physical actuators and autonomous controllers become increasingly exposed to network-borne cyber threats. This paper explores hardware-level security mechanisms (TPM, TrustZone, HSM), low-latency embedded operating systems, encrypted network protocols (TLS/DTLS), threat modeling, and defensive architectures designed to protect modern industrial, medical, and autonomous systems.

title: Digital twin technology for HIV patient virtual modeling: a novel approach to treatment optimization
abstract: Background: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection remains a global health challenge, necessitating personalized treatment strategies to optimize patient outcomes. Digital twin technology-synchronized with real-world entities-offers a pathway to precision medicine in HIV care. Methods: We analyzed 5,436 HIV patients (2016-2024) with demographic, immunologic, and antiretroviral therapy (ART) information. Core algorithms comprised gradient boosting and random forest ensembles; deep architectures (LSTM and Transformer networks) were evaluated as comparative benchmarks on longitudinal feature tensors under identical supervision. Models used five-fold cross-validation, regularization, dropout, and early stopping. A probabilistic treatment ranking layer generated diversified regimen suggestions conditioned on model outputs. Results: up to 0.97; cross-validation stability reported in the Results). Deep models achieved comparable held-out accuracy on the same endpoint; the ranking module produced balanced regimen distributions in an illustrative optimization cohort. Simulated digital twin scenarios demonstrated counterfactual CD4 projections under alternative ART strategies for low, moderate, and higher baseline immunology profiles. Discussion: The specific contribution is an explicit patient-state → prediction → regimen exploration pipeline suited to integration with telehealth analytics (risk dashboards, adherence supports), while transparently acknowledging endpoint and leakage limitations and the need for prospective outcome validation. A pragmatic HIV treatment optimization strategy is to route model-supported prioritization into clinician-facing dashboards and remote monitoring workflows rather than autonomous prescribing.

title: Automated Researchers Can Mitigate Well-characterized Alignment Failures
abstract: Automating alignment research may accelerate progress toward aligned AI, but whether it does is hard to measure. Luckily, many alignment failures, such as deception, sycophancy, and jailbreaks, are already measurable by public benchmarks. We study whether automated alignment researchers (AARs) can post-train to mitigate alignment failures by proposing training methods and data to simultaneously optimize multiple safety benchmarks, while largely preserving general capability. Across 10 alignment failures, the strongest AAR methods significantly reduce the targeted alignment failures and generalize to a held-out benchmark, multi-turn behavioral audits, and models up to 4.7x larger than the target model. As a human baseline, 28 experienced researchers receive up to eight hours to develop one-shot methods for the same benchmarks, but their methods underperform the best AAR methods. Using human ideas as the AARs' initial research direction does not improve performance, suggesting current AARs may not need guidance from experienced researchers. These results suggest that automating alignment research on well-characterized failures may be practical in the near term.

title: AcrossVAM1.0: Particle World Modeling for Text-Assisted Robot Video Prediction
abstract: Predicting robot videos requires both precise motion reasoning and preservation of high-frequency appearance, yet monolithic pixel models entangle these objectives and often conceal their progress behind a strong last-frame baseline. We present AcrossVAM1.0, a lightweight, text-assisted video action model that factorizes future prediction into object-centric motion and dense appearance. A frozen SAM3-DLP codec decomposes four context frames into semantic particles for the robot, arm, and gripper, together with a background latent. A 0.28M-parameter spatio-temporal Transformer aligns particle identities, rolls their states forward, and is modulated by a frozen OpenCLIP instruction embedding through FiLM. A causal dual-stream decoder combines particle-rendered motion with appearance encoded exclusively from the last observed frame; a residual refiner and learned delivery mask produce five future frames without access to future appearance. On our VRS benchmark constructed from diverse real-robot trajectories, particle dynamics reduce trajectory error by 21.0\% over persistence. evidence.title: AcrossVAM1.0: Particle World Modeling for Text-Assisted Robot Video Prediction
evidence.abstract: Predicting robot videos requires both precise motion reasoning and preservation of high-frequency appearance, yet monolithic pixel models entangle these objectives and often conceal their progress behind a strong last-frame baseline. title: Focus Where It Counts: A Salience-Driven Vision-Language Model for Low Vision Assistance
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are rapidly progressing and offer promising capabilities for assistive technologies supporting persons with blindness or low vision. However, existing VLMs are primarily designed for general-purpose captioning and do not explicitly model human perceptual priorities, thereby limiting their ability to emphasize the most relevant information in a scene. To address this gap, we propose a salience-driven captioning framework that prioritizes scene elements according to their importance for human-centered assistance. We curate three salience-aware datasets, namely, Salience COCO, Salience Flickr, and Salience VizWiz, with object-level salience annotations designed to reflect the visual information most relevant to low vision users across different environments. Building on these datasets, we introduce Salience-LLaVA, a salience-aware VLM that incorporates salience cues to generate captions in which important elements are mentioned in the order of importance. Our work makes four main contributions. We build salience-aware datasets verified by low vision participants, propose Salience-LLaVA to describe objects in the order of importance, introduce SCMI to evaluate ordering accuracy, and deploy the system on assistive glasses to demonstrate real-world practicality. Code and datasets are available at: https://github.com/topo-focus/Topofocus

title: Entangled States are Typically Incomparable
abstract: Abstract Consider a bipartite quantum system, where Alice and Bob jointly possess a pure state $$|\psi \rangle $$ | ψ ⟩ . Using local quantum operations on their respective subsystems, and unlimited classical communication, Alice and Bob may be able to transform $$|\psi \rangle $$ | ψ ⟩ into another state $$|\phi \rangle $$ | ϕ ⟩ . Famously, Nielsen’s theorem [28] provides a necessary and sufficient algebraic criterion for such a transformation to be possible (namely, the entanglement spectrum of $$|\phi \rangle $$ | ϕ ⟩ should majorise the entanglement spectrum of $$|\psi \rangle $$ | ψ ⟩ ). In the paper where Nielsen proved this theorem, he conjectured that in the limit of large dimensionality, for almost all pairs of states $$|\psi \rangle , |\phi \rangle $$ | ψ ⟩ , | ϕ ⟩ (according to the natural unitary invariant measure) such a transformation is not possible. That is to say, typical pairs of quantum states $$|\psi \rangle , |\phi \rangle $$ | ψ ⟩ , | ϕ ⟩ are entangled in fundamentally different ways, that cannot be converted to each other via local operations and classical communication. Via Nielsen’s theorem, this conjecture can be equivalently stated as a conjecture about majorisation of spectra of random matrices from the so-called trace-normalised complex Wishart–Laguerre ensemble . Concretely, let X and Y be independent $$n \times m$$ n × m random matrices whose entries are i.i.d. standard complex Gaussians; then Nielsen’s conjecture says that the probability that the spectrum of $$X X^\dagger / \operatorname {tr}(X X^\dagger )$$ X X † / tr ( X X † ) majorises the spectrum of $$Y Y^\dagger / \operatorname {tr}(Y Y^\dagger )$$ Y Y † / tr ( Y Y † ) tends to zero as both n and m grow large. We prove this conjecture, and we also confirm some related predictions of Cunden et al. [12].

title: Technology foresight applied to the use of artificial intelligence in marketing strategies: a systematic review
abstract: La presente investigación analiza la transición de los paradigmas tradicionales de marketing hacia un modelo estrategia empresarial mediado por Inteligencia Artificial (IA). En un entorno caracterizado por la volatilidad y la complejidad del comportamiento del consumidor, la gestión estratégica exige evolucionar desde la asistencia operativa hacia arquitecturas más avanzadas. A través de una revisión sistemática de literatura y un análisis transversal de seis dimensiones críticas: segmentación, personalización, precios, customer journey, producto y canales, se demuestra que la implementación de la IA reduce la entropía en la toma de decisiones y optimiza indicadores clave como por ejemplo el costo de adquisición de clientes. El estudio concluye que el éxito de esta transformación no reside en la automatización absoluta, sino en un modelo de "Aumentación Humana", donde el juicio experto actúa como un filtro ético y estratégico. Finalmente, se propone un cuadro de mando integral, el cual integra cuatro perspectivas fundamentales para el éxito organizacional como lo son la perspectiva financiera, la relación con los clientes, la gestión de procesos internos y el desarrollo del talento humano que constituye la empresa.

title: Mixtures of Polynomial With Tails as Probability Distributions: Theoretical and Experimental Evaluation
abstract: Bayesian networks based on mixtures of polynomials (MoPs) are used to model multivariate hybrid or continuous probability distributions. MoPs provide a flexible yet simple model to deal with probabilistic reasoning, approximating complex or empirical probability distributions. We review the main models based on MoPs in the literature, introducing an alternative MoP approach: the mixtures of polynomials with tails (tMoPs). Also, we present procedures for learning tMoP marginal and conditional densities from data. This learning algorithms are tested with many well-known probability distributions. In these experiments, the tMoP models yield satisfactory results in comparison to other techniques, including other available MoPs alternatives. We also propose a meta-model that can directly, using interpolation, provide a tMoP expression for a specific density within a given family. This idea is tested with several probability distributions of one and two parameters, giving promising results.

title: The Quantum Pi Benchmark: Cross-Provider Portability and Boundaries for Standardization
abstract: The Quantum Pi Benchmark (QPB) separates oracle-construction provenance, controller blindness, demonstrated capability, execution layer, and provider access rather than compressing them into a vendor score. This paper tests whether the architecture-neutral information flow established in the Benchmark can be carried through additional provider stacks, using Microsoft Azure’s platform, and records the point at which each accessible path stops. The frozen record contains 20 accepted analysis rows mapped to 16 unique jobs: fourteen Rigetti ideal Quantum Virtual Machine (QVM) jobs and two Quantinuum H2-1E noisy-emulator jobs. It contains zero quantum processing unit (QPU) jobs. The Rigetti campaign implements an N = 4, one-iteration search and an eight-job control suite through logical Quil and Azure-hosted quilc/QVM. Six candidate circuits return the marked address in 256/256 shots; matched-search and no-hit controls remain near the 1/4 reference, two Ramsey controls return their expected event in 1,024/1,024 shots, and four basis roundtrips return 1,024/1,024. The evidence supports P3/B0 validation but no hardware rung or hardware-evidence claim. The Quantinuum campaign validates all sixteen finite Bailey–Borwein–Plouffe (BBP) arithmetic trajectories, compiles N = 16 provenance class 3 / blindness class 0 / capability-rung 5 (P3/B0/R5)-candidate circuits into an H2-native basis, audits provider Open Quantum Assembly Language (OpenQASM) transport, and executes them on H2-1E. Native compilation expanded depth from 464 to 5,856 and produced 6,614–11,568 ZZPhase gates. Search target frequencies were 1/32 and 0/16 against the ideal 0.90845, while the compute–uncompute roundtrip returned the expected all-zero state in 0/16 shots. These eligible negative outcomes locate an execution boundary on the tested circuit-and-model path without implying an H2 hardware result. These results support the feasibility of QPB interrogation across differently designed provider stacks.

title: Derived Results and Figure/Table Source Data for Hypocentral Depth and Stress Regime Improve Deep-Learning Forecasts of Spatial Seismicity
abstract: This dataset provides the compact source tables and arrays supporting the figures and tables in the manuscript “Hypocentral Depth and Stress Regime Improve Deep-Learning Forecasts of Spatial Seismicity.” It includes study-region boundaries and WSM2025 record counts, sample compositions and results for 23 random-forest tasks, nine retained ConvLSTM runs for five model configurations, predicted-positive area statistics, prediction-frequency grids, and CSI robustness summaries. title: A Functional Programming Language for Multi-Variable Differentiable Functions
abstract: This paper introduces a novel functional programming language designed specifically to facilitate the computation and optimization of multi-variable differentiable functions. The core concept revolves around seamlessly integrating gradient calculation and optimization capabilities within a functional paradigm. Unlike traditional approaches that often necessitate procedural coding and manual differentiation, this language provides an automated system for computing derivatives and supports the implementation of various optimization algorithms. The primary benefit lies in the simplification of the optimization workflow and a significant improvement in development efficiency. This document details the design and key features of the language, focusing on its core mechanisms and illustrating how it addresses the need for a more intuitive and efficient approach to multi-variable optimization within a functional programming context. The language utilizes a declarative style, emphasizing function definitions and transformations rather than imperative step-by-step instructions. This allows for a more concise and less error-prone representation of mathematical operations, particularly those involving derivatives.

title: Cognitive Mapping for Knowledge Representation and Reasoning
abstract: This paper explores the application of cognitive mapping as a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning. Traditional knowledge representation methods often struggle to capture the complex, interconnected nature of human understanding. Cognitive mapping, inspired by how humans organize and process information, offers a promising alternative. This work proposes a framework utilizing graph-based representations to model knowledge, leveraging graph algorithms for inference and problem-solving. The core claim is that by explicitly representing knowledge as a cognitive map, we can effectively simulate human cognitive processes and achieve robust solutions to complex problems. The proposed mechanism involves constructing a cognitive map model, transforming knowledge into a graph structure, and employing graph algorithms for inference. The significance lies in its ability to mimic human cognition, offering potential advantages over traditional symbolic AI approaches. This paper outlines the key components of the framework, explores potential applications, and discusses future research directions.

title: Hyperdimensional Computing with Neural Symbology
abstract: This paper proposes a novel computational paradigm combining hyperdimensional computing (HDC) with neural symbology. HDC leverages high-dimensional vectors (hypervectors) for efficient data storage and similarity comparison, while neural symbology provides a framework for learning symbolic representations. The core claim is that integrating these two approaches can lead to a fundamentally new and powerful AI system. We outline the core mechanism, which involves mapping hypervectors to symbolic concepts using neural networks. This approach offers the potential for energy-efficient and scalable AI, addressing limitations of traditional deep learning methods. The paper details the mathematical framework, focusing on vector representations, similarity measures, and neural network architectures. We explore the advantages of this hybrid approach, highlighting its suitability for tasks requiring both numerical and symbolic processing. The research demonstrates a promising direction for future AI development.

title: Shaping Gradient and Exploration-Noise Initialization, Not Reward Polarity, Determine Convergence in Deep Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Quadrotor Navigation and Obstacle Avoidance
abstract: This paper presents a systematic reward engineering methodology for training a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) quadrotor navigation policy in the Webots simulator, using a hierarchical architecture in which a PID controller handles low-level stabilization and a PPO policy issues velocity commands. We document the complete evolution of a composite ten-term reward function across seven versions (v5 through v11) and retrain the key versions with multiple independent training seeds. The multi-seed study revises the single-seed history: penalty-dominated configurations (v8, v10) fail across all seeds, while the strongest historical version proves seed-sensitive (v11: 32.2 +/− 15.8%). An ablation removing the continuous distance-shaping term from v11 yields 0% success across seven seeds, identifying that term as necessary for convergence. We further isolate a previously hidden co-factor: with the library-default exploration-noise initialization (sigma_0 = 1.0), sampled actions saturate the bounded action space, the exploration variance receives no learning gradient, and curriculum progression deadlocks regardless of reward design; initializing sigma_0 = 0.37 restores gradient flow. With this correction and a deterministic evaluation-gated curriculum, the final configuration is evaluated across the full curriculum rather than at a single operating point: across five independent training seeds under a deterministic protocol, it attains 95.0% ± 6.2% navigation success at Stage 0 conditions (2 m targets, no obstacles), 89.6% ± 6.9% at Stage 1 conditions (4 m, one obstacle), and 48.4% ± 10.8% at Stage 2 conditions (7 m, three obstacles). Reporting this difficulty curve, rather than a single headline value, exposes a substantial generalization gap whose dominant failure mode is obstacle collision (45–52% of episodes at Stage 2). Matched retraining of Soft Actor-Critic and TD3 baselines under identical reward and curriculum conditions yields one completed seed each both baselines show non-monotonic difficulty curves, and at Stage 2 conditions, TD3 (64.0%) exceeds PPO (48.4% ± 10.8%) while SAC (43.0%) falls just below it, whereas at Stage 0, PPO (95.0%) leads both, so the ranking is operating point-dependent on the current single-seed evidence. We conclude that a continuous shaping gradient and the exploration-noise initialization, interacting with the curriculum advancement criterion, determine convergence in continuous control deep reinforcement learning, and that reward polarity by itself does not.

title: Endostrat: a multicenter study of AI-assisted two-level risk stratification for gastric precancerous and early neoplastic lesion screening
abstract: Background In large-scale endoscopic screening, neoplastic lesions constitute only a small fraction of the cases examined, making detection susceptible to reader fatigue. Most existing AI systems rely on image-level annotations and single-stage classification, limiting patient-level assessment and safety-aware review prioritization. We developed and validated EndoStrat, a two-stage AI-assisted risk stratification system that triages low-risk patients and prioritizes high-risk patients for focused endoscopic review. Methods This retrospective, multicenter study included 8,829 patients (approximately 220,000 white-light endoscopic images) from three centers with distinct pathological compositions. Patients were classified into four categories: normal/superficial gastritis, atrophic gastritis/intestinal metaplasia (Atrophy/IM), low-grade intraepithelial neoplasia (LGIN), and high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia/early gastric cancer (HGIN/EGC). Center 1 was split into a training cohort ( n = 3,555) and an internal validation cohort ( n = 890); Center 2 ( n = 2,896) and Center 3 ( n = 1,488) served as independent external validation cohorts. EndoStrat employs a Level-1 screening module that triages patients into low-risk and review-required groups using patient-level weak supervision and a Level-2 stratification module that outputs a continuous risk score integrating image features with age and sex for priority-based review. Two comparison methods—an image-level classifier and a four-class multiple instance learning classifier—were evaluated under identical conditions. Results Across the three validation cohorts, Level 1 achieved AUCs of 0.770, 0.720, and 0.674, which were numerically higher than those of both comparators. At the exact fixed operating threshold of 0.22, the HGIN/EGC flag rate was 93.0% or higher in all cohorts, and the neoplasia miss rate ranged from 5.8% to 8.1%. Among patients with normal/superficial pathology, 21.1%–26.1% were classified as low risk; across all patients, the corresponding overall low-risk assignment rates ranged from 11.2% to 19.6%. In a module-level analysis including all patients with pathology other than Normal/Superficial irrespective of Level-1 classification, the Level-2 continuous risk score showed a clear monotonic gradient across Atrophy/IM, LGIN, and HGIN/EGC (all p < 0.001), with concordance indices of 0.907–0.967 after clinical features were incorporated. Conclusions EndoStrat showed consistent risk-stratification performance across three validation cohorts with different pathological compositions. These retrospective findings suggest that EndoStrat may have potential to support risk-based review prioritization while retaining a high proportion of neoplastic cases in the review-required group. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine its effects on clinical workflow, diagnostic performance, and patient outcomes.

We developed and validated EndoStrat, a two-stage AI-assisted risk stratification system that triages low-risk patients and prioritizes high-risk patients for focused endoscopic review. Methods This retrospective, multicenter study included 8,829 patients (approximately 220,000 white-light endoscopic images) from three centers with distinct pathological compositions. Patients were classified into four categories: normal/superficial gastritis, atrophic gastritis/intestinal metaplasia (Atrophy/IM), low-grade intraepithelial neoplasia (LGIN), and high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia/early gastric cancer (HGIN/EGC). Center 1 was split into a training cohort ( n = 3,555) and an internal validation cohort ( n = 890); Center 2 ( n = 2,896) and Center 3 ( n = 1,488) served as independent external validation cohorts. EndoStrat employs a Level-1 screening module that triages patients into low-risk and review-required groups using patient-level weak supervision and a Level-2 stratification module that outputs a continuous risk score integrating image features with age and sex for priority-based review. Two comparison methods—an image-level classifier and a four-class multiple instance learning classifier—were evaluated under identical conditions. Results Across the three validation cohorts, Level 1 achieved AUCs of 0.770, 0.720, and 0.674, which were numerically higher than those of both comparators. At the exact fixed operating threshold of 0.22, the HGIN/EGC flag rate was 93.0% or higher in all cohorts, and the neoplasia miss rate ranged from 5.8% to 8.1%. Among patients with normal/superficial pathology, 21.1%–26.1% were classified as low risk; across all patients, the corresponding overall low-risk assignment rates ranged from 11.2% to 19.6%. In a module-level analysis including all patients with pathology other than Normal/Superficial irrespective of Level-1 classification, the Level-2 continuous risk score showed a clear monotonic gradient across Atrophy/IM, LGIN, and HGIN/EGC (all p < 0.001), with concordance indices of 0.907–0.967 after clinical features were incorporated. Conclusions EndoStrat showed consistent risk-stratification performance across three validation cohorts with different pathological compositions. These retrospective findings suggest that EndoStrat may have potential to support risk-based review prioritization while retaining a high proportion of neoplastic cases in the review-required group. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine its effects on clinical workflow, diagnostic performance, and patient outcomes.

title: Адаптивная гибридная нейросетевая архитектура на основе внимания для идентификации дикторов в корпоративных совещаниях
abstract: Актуальность исследования обусловлена ростом потребности в автоматизации ведения протоколов корпоративных встреч, которое является трудоёмким и затяжным процессом, сопровождающимся высоким риском ошибок. Современные системы распознавания речи (ASR –Automatic Speech Recognition) работают нестабильно при многопользовательских диалогах, перекрытиях голосовых фрагментов, фоновом шуме и использовании специализированной лексики. Особенно остро стоит проблема распознавания дикторов (Speaker Identification, SID), когда на одного сотрудника приходится мало эталонных записей, что вполне типично для офисной среды. Дополнительные трудности создаёт и акустическая обстановка: гулкие кабинеты, одновременные высказывания, отсутствие чёткого разделения голосов. Таким образом, цель данной работы – создание гибридной нейросетевой модели для точной транскрипции и надёжной атрибуции речи в групповых дискуссиях. В рамках работы проанализированы слабые места ASR-систем и методов SID, предложена трёхуровневая архитектура: сегментация аудиопотока VAD + SCD (VAD – Voice Activity Detection – определение активности речи), SCD – Speaker Change Detection – детектирование смены диктора), идентификация по голосовым эмбеддингам с механизмом внимания к эталонам, транскрибация[1]с учётом личности говорящего, так же приведено математическое обоснование ключевых компонентов. Теоретическая значимость заключается в построении методики SID на основе механизма внимания, позволяющая эффективно решать задачи обучения с малым числом примеров (few-shot learning). В отличие от традиционных подходов, требующих обширных размеченных корпусов, новая архитектура учится сопоставлять речевые фрагменты с небольшим числом эталонных записей. Эффективность метода эмпирически подтверждена на реальных записях корпоративных совещаний (свыше 20 часов, пять участников). Модуль сегментации показал F1-меру VAD на уровне 0,885, а модуль идентификации диктора точность 62,5%, что в трое выше случайного уровня (20%). Транскрибация выполнена через внешнюю систему Whisper, гарантирующую высокую достоверность распознавания. Результаты позволяют построить систему автоматического ведения протоколов совещаний, а архитектура позволяет работать и с большим числом участников, а также легко адаптируется под разные форматы коммуникаций: от переговоров до встреч с участием клиентов. Функциональные возможности гибридной нейросетевой модели могут быть использованы при создании различных инструментов для протоколирования корпоративных встреч. The relevance of this research stems from the growing need to automate corporate meeting minutes, a labor-intensive and time-consuming process with a high risk of errors. Current speech recognition systems (ASR – Automatic Speech Recognition) perform poorly in multi-user conversations, with overlapping voices, background noise, and the use of specialized vocabulary. Speaker identification (SID – Speaker Identification) is particularly challenging when there are few reference recordings per employee, which is typical in an office environment. Acoustic environments also pose additional challenges: echoing offices, simultaneous speech, and poor voice separation. Therefore, the goal of this study is to develop a hybrid neural network model for accurate transcription and reliable speech attribution in group discussions. This paper analyzes the weaknesses of ASR systems and SID methods and proposes a three-tier architecture: audio stream segmentation (VAD – Voice Activity Detection, SCD – Speaker Change Detection), voice embedding identification with a reference attention mechanism, and speaker-aware transcription. A mathematical justification for the key components is also provided. The theoretical significance lies in the development of an attention-based SID method that effectively solves few-shot learning problems. Unlike traditional approaches that require large labeled corpora, the new architecture learns to match speech fragments with a small number of reference recordings. The effectiveness of the method has been empirically confirmed using real corporate meeting recordings (over 20 hours, five participants). The segmentation module demonstrated a VAD F1 score of 0.885, and the speaker identification module achieved an accuracy of 62.5%, which is three times higher than chance (20%). Transcription was performed using the external Whisper system, which guarantees high recognition accuracy. The results enable the development of a system for automatic meeting minutes, and the architecture supports a large number of participants and is easily adapted to various communication formats: from negotiations to client meetings. The functionality of the hybrid neural network model can be used to create various tools for corporate meeting minutes.

title: Oculi: A Conversational Agentic Platform for Automated Credit Risk Analysis
abstract: Credit risk analysis in financial institutions traditionally requires analysts to manually write SQL queries, run statistical computations, and build visualization dashboards. This is a time-consuming workflow that limits exploration to familiar segments. We introduce \textbf{Oculi}, a conversational platform that transforms natural language questions into comprehensive credit risk analyses, complete with data queries, statistical testing, and interactive visualizations. Oculi employs a three-layer architecture that separates reasoning (LLM-powered agent), execution (Model Context Protocol tool servers), and presentation (agentic UI), enabling analysts to discover high-risk portfolio segments. Within Oculi, a new segment discovery pipeline is proposed that combines deterministic statistical methods with LLM-guided feature selection, leveraging LLM semantic domain knowledge alongside data-driven metrics to identify meaningful, actionable portfolio segments. Evaluated on a mortgage portfolio with 200+ features, Oculi demonstrates effectiveness in discovering material risk segments previously intractable through manual exploration, reducing time-to-insight significantly while maintaining auditability and statistical rigor.

title: LLM-Based Agents for Software and Systems Security: Approaches, Applications, and Assessment
abstract: Software and systems security workflows are typically procedural: analysts inspect heterogeneous artifacts, form hypotheses, invoke tools, interpret outputs, and revise plans. Large language model (LLM)-based agents, which can plan, use tools, retain state, and revise actions across multi-step workflows, are being rapidly adopted to automate this work. Given the consequences of delegating security decisions to autonomous systems, understanding how such agents are built, used, and assessed is crucial. Yet to this date, there remains a lack of systematic understanding of what has been done and how far we are in this field: the term "agent" is applied inconsistently, applications differ sharply in risk, and assessment protocols are often incomparable. To gain a comprehensive and coherent view of this area hence inform relevant future research, this paper provides a systematic literature review of the (1) technical approaches, including agent architecture, perception, memory, reasoning and planning, action space, orchestration, and self-improvement, (2) applications, with respect to the security tasks served, and (3) assessment, including the datasets, outcome and trajectory metrics, safety measures, and baselines considered, over the peer-reviewed literature spanning the emergence of this area (2023--2026). Our synthesis reveals a field that has built agents able to act but not yet agents whose authority is bounded or whose behavior is auditable. In addition to knowledge systematization, we also extend our insights into the limitations of and challenges faced by current approach, application, and assessment designs, which shed light on potentially promising future research directions.

title: Structural cryptanalysis and storage efficiency of Kronecker-product diffusion layers for lightweight block ciphers
abstract: Matrix-based linear transformations are fundamental to the diffusion properties of modern block ciphers. This paper investigates the algebraic structure and security of the Dual-Matrix Affine Modular construction \(C\equiv K_LMK_R+K_S\pmod p.\) Although it is structurally isomorphic to a constrained affine map on \(\mathbb{Z}_p^{n^2}\) via the Kronecker product \(K_R^T\otimes K_L\), this construction offers a significant efficiency advantage: it reduces the storage complexity from \(\mathcal{O}(n^4)\) (for a generic linear layer) to \(\mathcal{O}(n^2)\). We formally derive the effective key space and present a rigorous structural chosen-plaintext attack. We prove that by exploiting the tensor decomposition property, an equivalent key tuple can be recovered in \(\mathcal{O}(n^4)\) field operations, significantly bypassing the \(\mathcal{O}(n^6)\) complexity of generic affine cryptanalysis. Our results demonstrate that while insecure as a standalone primitive, this structure offers a favorable trade-off between large-state diffusion and implementation cost, making it a compelling candidate for the mixing layer in lightweight Substitution-Permutation Networks (SPNs).

title: Scaling Multilingual mT5 Models with English Intermediate-Task Training for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Performance
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: What is the impact of scaling the size of multilingual mT5 models with English intermediate-task training on zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance across different XTREME-R tasks, measured by accuracy and F1 scores? title: Scalable Quantum Simulation of Molecular Dynamics using Tensor Networks
abstract: Quantum simulation offers a pathway to accurately model and understand complex molecular systems, a task often intractable using classical computational methods. However, the computational cost of simulating quantum systems, particularly those involving many particles and complex interactions, remains a significant barrier. This work presents a novel approach leveraging tensor network methods to achieve scalable quantum simulation of molecular dynamics. We demonstrate how tensor networks can efficiently represent the quantum state of a molecular system, allowing for the accurate calculation of its dynamics. The core idea is to utilize the tensor network representation to reduce the computational complexity associated with traditional quantum simulation algorithms. The presented method offers a promising route toward simulating larger and more realistic molecular systems, opening up new possibilities in fields such as drug discovery, materials science, and fundamental physics. This paper details the theoretical framework and provides a conceptual outline, emphasizing the scalability of the approach.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Cryptographic Key Distribution via Entanglement Swapping
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to enhancing cryptographic key distribution using entanglement swapping. Current quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols are often limited by distance due to signal loss and decoherence during the direct transmission of entangled photons. This research proposes a protocol that overcomes these limitations by employing entanglement swapping, effectively extending the range of secure key exchange. The core of the method involves strategically swapping entangled pairs to create correlated states between distant parties, circumventing the need for direct transmission over long distances. Mathematical formulations detailing the protocol's key steps, including the quantum operations and measurement outcomes, are presented. The analysis demonstrates a pathway towards significantly increasing the practical range of QKD systems, offering a potential solution for secure communication over greater distances. The theoretical framework presented here lays the groundwork for future experimental implementations and further optimization of entanglement swapping protocols for enhanced QKD performance.

title: Adaptive Neural Network Topology via Relational Graph Embeddings
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neural network design, termed Adaptive Neural Network Topology via Relational Graph Embeddings. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the network's topology during training, moving beyond fixed architectures. We achieve this by learning a relational graph embedding of the network's connections, capturing dependencies between neurons. This embedding is then utilized to guide the growth or pruning of connections, facilitating efficient knowledge transfer and adaptation to complex datasets. The method leverages graph neural networks (GNNs) to derive these embeddings, providing a mechanism for intelligent structural adaptation. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a theoretical analysis and a detailed exploration of the underlying principles. The key innovation lies in the integration of graph learning with dynamic network topology control, offering a potentially more efficient and robust training paradigm. The proposed method addresses the limitations of traditional, static neural network architectures, particularly in scenarios with evolving data distributions or complex relationships within the data. Experimental validation, while not included in this paper, would further demonstrate the advantages of this adaptive topology approach.

The method leverages graph neural networks (GNNs) to derive these embeddings, providing a mechanism for intelligent structural adaptation. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a theoretical analysis and a detailed exploration of the underlying principles. The key innovation lies in the integration of graph learning with dynamic network topology control, offering a potentially more efficient and robust training paradigm. The proposed method addresses the limitations of traditional, static neural network architectures, particularly in scenarios with evolving data distributions or complex relationships within the data. Experimental validation, while not included in this paper, would further demonstrate the advantages of this adaptive topology approach.

title: Meta-Learning-Based Domain Adaptation Transfer Learning - MLDATL
abstract: This paper investigates the application of meta-learning techniques to domain adaptation transfer learning (DTATL). The core claim is that meta-learning can significantly enhance a model's ability to adapt to new domains, thereby improving the efficiency and effectiveness of the transfer learning process. The proposed method, MLDATL, leverages meta-learning to train a model capable of rapid adaptation to novel domains. This model is then employed in a domain adaptation transfer learning framework. Unlike traditional DTATL methods which typically require substantial domain-specific data, MLDATL aims to reduce this data dependency through the use of meta-learned representations. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach and present a framework for implementation, demonstrating the potential of meta-learning to address the challenges inherent in domain adaptation. The primary focus is on the learning of adaptable features and the optimization of transfer learning strategies. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in adaptation speed and accuracy compared to conventional DTATL approaches.

title: An exhaustive prescribed LP(99) search
abstract: This dataset records an exhaustive computational search for Legendre pairs of length 99, written LP(99), within one explicitly defined prescribed representative population. Here, “exhaustive” refers only to that population; this is not an unrestricted census of all LP(99) pairs. Prescribed search domain. For a sign row x = (x_0,...,x_98), its 9-fold compression to length 11 is C_j(x) = Σ_{k=0}^8 x_{j+11k}, for j = 0,...,10. The ordered compressed pair is fixed as A = (1, 3, -3, 3, 3, 3, -3, -3, -3, 3, -3) and B = (1, -3, 3, -3, -3, -3, 3, 3, 3, -3, 3). The prescription-preserving symmetry group uses a common unit decimation d modulo 99, independent shifts a,b in 11Z/99Z, and a row swap when d is a quadratic nonresidue modulo 11; its order is 4,860. The labelled input contains 15,083,874 admissible length-33 intermediate pairs. Canonicalization gives 83,879 ordered pair-orbit ranks, numbered 0 through 83,878, and stabilizer canonicalization gives 143,408,299 final scope representatives. The technical note states the canonicalization and stabilizer rules. Scholarly context. This prescribed length-11 compression is the p = 11, q = 3 case of the q²-uncompression framework and Conjecture 3.3 in Ilias S. Kotsireas, Ana Isabel Gómez, and Domingo Gómez-Pérez, “On properties of Legendre pairs under compression,” Proceedings of ISSAC 2025, pp. 79–86, DOI 10.1145/3747199.3747549. The canonical census, exhaustive search, and verification deposited here were developed and executed independently. Result. The 68 gap-free coverage rows record 26,881,720,674,613,832 evaluations across every pair-orbit rank. Exactly one join hit occurred, in chapter 7. It is an exact LP(99) pair and yields a Hadamard matrix of order 200, H(200), by the bordered two-circulant construction. Its prescription-preserving affine orbit has size 4,860 and trivial stabilizer; these orbit members are not additional hits or inequivalent classes. Compute cost. The sealed receipts sum the store and stream kernels to 417,778.02 single-worker hours, approximately 417,778 core-hours or 47.7 core-years. The campaign elapsed over 14 days, 22 hours, 1 minute, and 15 seconds. This core-hour total excludes merging, orchestration, staging, verification, and idle time. Package and verification. The 280,960-byte ZIP is a ten-file compact evidence package containing a two-page technical note and its TeX source, a reusable style file, the exact LP(99) pair, the 68-row coverage table, the canonical result record, SHA-256 checksums, licensing terms, a README, and a standalone Python verifier. After extraction, run: python3 -B verify.py . The verifier checks the closed file census and hashes, gap-free coverage and totals, LP(99) row sums and periodic autocorrelations, all 40,000 entries of the H(200) Gram matrix, and the affine orbit. Scope and audit limit. This package proves exhaustiveness only for the prescribed representative population defined above. It proves no result for LP(333) or Hadamard matrices of order 668. The ZIP is not the complete 13.9 GB receipt archive and does not rerun every candidate evaluation or independently establish historical processor execution. The retained full archive has SHA-256 b569b7c8dbf9e265b59f8447790693d87db0f3dcbd1628aa5158c350cc28e2f1 and replays 3,035,920 authenticated summaries; independent confirmation requires a fresh campaign. Package SHA-256: a15dd8773a202c7210c7a84648b0bf4c8fc143cb94eddbdbefe614f9dd22eb45. The included technical note records the generative-AI disclosure and author-responsibility statement.

title: Multimodal Intermediate-Task Training for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer in XTREME-R
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Can multimodal intermediate-task training (e.g., text-image tasks) enhance zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance on the XTREME-R benchmark compared to text-only intermediate tasks, as evaluated by accuracy and F1-score? title: Personale Wirkungsrückkopplung in longitudinaler Mensch–KI-Interaktion
abstract: Die wiederholte Nutzung dialogischer generativer KI erzeugt nicht nur Outputs, sondern kann auch Erfahrungen darüber hervorbringen, wie unterschiedliche Formen der Mensch–KI-Interaktion auf die eigene kognitive, epistemische oder handlungsbezogene Funktionsweise wirken. Bestehende Forschung untersucht bereits Prompt Adaptation, metakognitive Regulation, Self-Regulated Learning, Trust Calibration, Human–AI Fit, Appropriation und Co-Adaptation. Weniger geklärt ist, wie wahrgenommene personale Wirkungen vorausgehender Interaktionen selbst zu Informationen für die bewusste Gestaltung späterer Mensch–KI-Interaktionen werden können. Das vorliegende theoretische Paper entwickelt hierfür das Modell personaler Wirkungsrückkopplung. Personale Wirkung bezeichnet eine Veränderung oder Zustandsdifferenz aufseiten des Menschen, zu deren Entstehung eine Mensch–KI-Interaktion beitragen kann. Das Modell unterscheidet diese Wirkung von ihrer subjektiven Wahrnehmung und berücksichtigt, dass ihre Bedeutung von den jeweils verfolgten Zielen abhängt. Werden wahrgenommene Wirkungen zumindest teilweise Eigenschaften einer Interaktionskonfiguration zugerechnet, können daraus subjektive Wirkungsannahmen entstehen: revidierbare Annahmen darüber, welche Formen der Mensch–KI-Interaktion unter bestimmten Bedingungen mit welchen personalen Wirkungen verbunden sein können. Solche Annahmen können spätere Interaktionskonfigurationen beeinflussen, indem bestimmte Interaktionsbedingungen gezielt verändert, beibehalten oder situationsbezogen gewählt werden. Die daraus entstehenden neuen Wirkungserfahrungen können frühere Wirkungsannahmen bestätigen, differenzieren oder revidieren. Der vorgeschlagene Prozess bildet eine longitudinale Rückkopplungsstruktur: Frühere personale Wirkung wird – sofern sie wahrgenommen, bewertet und interaktional attribuiert wird – zu einer möglichen Bedingung späterer Interaktionsgestaltung; die Wirkungen dieser rekonfigurierten Interaktion erzeugen wiederum neue Evidenz. Über wiederholte Episoden kann daraus ein zunehmend differenziertes, ziel- und kontextspezifisches Repertoire der Interaktionsgestaltung hervorgehen. Aus dem Modell werden sechs empirisch prüfbare Propositionen abgeleitet. Der theoretische Beitrag liegt nicht in der allgemeinen Annahme erfahrungsbasierter oder rekursiver Anpassung von Mensch–KI-Interaktion. Er liegt in der Spezifikation eines engeren Rückkopplungspfades, in dem wahrgenommene personale Wirkungen vorausgehender Interaktionskonfigurationen zu subjektiven Wirkungsannahmen beitragen und als mögliche zielrelative Informationsgrundlage für die bewusste Gestaltung späterer Interaktionen relevant werden.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Temporal Constraints
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neuro-symbolic programming that addresses the critical limitation of lacking temporal reasoning. Existing neuro-symbolic systems primarily focus on static program generation, neglecting the crucial aspect of execution timing and temporal constraints. We introduce a framework that seamlessly integrates a temporal logic engine with a neural network, allowing the network to learn and satisfy precise timing requirements during program execution. The core mechanism involves training the neural network to translate high-level symbolic representations into executable code while simultaneously adhering to temporal constraints expressed in temporal logic. This approach enables the creation of temporally aware AI systems capable of complex tasks requiring precise timing, opening new avenues for applications in robotics, control systems, and other domains where temporal accuracy is paramount. The system's ability to learn these constraints directly from data, rather than relying on hand-engineered rules, represents a significant advancement in the field. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this method through a theoretical framework and outline potential future research directions. ---

title: Adaptive Code Generation via Evolutionary Programming with Formal Specifications
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to adaptive code generation that leverages the strengths of evolutionary programming and formal specifications. The core idea is to create an evolutionary algorithm that not only evaluates code based on its functional correctness but also incorporates formal verification to guarantee adherence to desired quality attributes. This integrated system dynamically adjusts the evolutionary process, prioritizing code variants that both satisfy functional requirements and exhibit desirable characteristics, such as low complexity and good performance. The research outlines a framework for this adaptive code generation system, highlighting the key components and their interactions. The system's ability to automatically refine code through a feedback loop based on formal verification provides a significant advancement over traditional code generation techniques, offering the potential for highly reliable and optimized software. The paper demonstrates the theoretical underpinnings of the approach and provides a conceptual design for its implementation.

title: Quantum-Inspired Random Walk Algorithms for Global Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-inspired concepts to enhance the performance of random walk algorithms, specifically within the domain of global optimization. Classical random walk algorithms frequently struggle with convergence issues, frequently becoming trapped within local optima, a significant limitation when dealing with complex, high-dimensional search spaces. This research proposes a novel approach where random walk behavior is modeled based on principles derived from quantum mechanics, incorporating superposition and interference effects to facilitate more extensive and efficient exploration of the solution landscape. The core idea is to replace the deterministic step size in traditional random walks with a probabilistic movement governed by a quantum-like probability distribution. We explore the mathematical formulation of this process, detailing the probabilities of transition between states and the impact of interference. The resulting algorithms demonstrate improved convergence rates and a reduced tendency to get stuck in local optima compared to standard random walk methods. The paper concludes by outlining potential future research directions, including adaptive parameter tuning and integration with other optimization techniques.

title: Information-Theoretic Limits on Graph Clustering
abstract: This paper investigates the inherent limits of graph clustering from an information-theoretic perspective. We argue that graph clustering fundamentally relies on compressing information regarding node relationships and propose that the information-theoretic limit provides a quantifiable measure of this redundancy. We derive a theoretical bound on achievable compression rates, leveraging concepts of mutual information and entropy, which is directly influenced by the graph's connectivity and node features. This work establishes a new framework for understanding graph clustering, offering a fundamental limit on clustering performance that can be used to evaluate and optimize clustering algorithms. The key contribution lies in shifting the focus from heuristic optimization to a rigorously defined, information-constrained objective.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Logic with Adaptive Rule Generation via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning by integrating neural networks and symbolic logic, dynamically refined through reinforcement learning. The core idea is to create a hybrid system capable of autonomously generating and adapting logical rules based on observational data, leading to more robust and explainable reasoning systems compared to traditional rule-based methods. We introduce a reinforcement learning agent tasked with iteratively modifying a knowledge base containing logical rules. A neural network acts as an evaluator, assessing the consistency and utility of proposed rule changes. This feedback loop enables the system to learn complex logical structures and adapt to evolving data. We demonstrate the potential of this approach in achieving greater adaptability and explainability in reasoning systems.

title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning via Counterfactual Reasoning
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has demonstrated remarkable success in solving complex tasks, yet its inherent opacity presents a significant challenge. The "black box" nature of RL agents hinders understanding, trust, and effective debugging. This work introduces a novel framework for Explainable Reinforcement Learning (XRL) that leverages counterfactual reasoning to provide transparent explanations of RL agent behavior. The core idea involves generating counterfactual scenarios – hypothetical situations where an agent's actions are altered – and analyzing the resulting changes in the agent's policy. We formalize this process with a mathematical representation, enabling systematic exploration of decision-making factors. This approach moves beyond simply visualizing agent behavior and offers a rigorous, interpretable method for understanding *why* an RL agent makes a particular decision. The framework's ability to highlight influential features and sensitivities is expected to improve agent design, enhance robustness, and ultimately, foster greater trust in RL systems. The key contributions include a formalization of counterfactual reasoning within the RL context and a methodology for generating and analyzing counterfactual scenarios. ---

abstract: Green SM: Taksi 100% Listrik adalah aplikasi transportasi daring digital yang digunakan untuk memberikan layanan moda transportasi mobil listrik yang digunakan berbagai kalangan guna membantu masyarakat dalam hal mobilisasi. Meskipun dikembangkan untuk tujuan yang baik, masih terdapat pengguna yang merasa kurang puas terhadap fitur layanan maupun performa dan kualitas layanan yang disediakan. Untuk memahami opini pengguna terhadap aplikasi ini, penelitian ini menerapkan metode Naive Bayes dengan meimplementasikan pelabelan InSet Lexicon-Based. Data penelitian diperoleh dari ulasan pengguna aplikasi Green SM: Taksi 100% Listrik di Google Play Store dengan kerangka kerja Knowledge Discovery in Database. Sebanyak 1000 ulasan, dengan data yang digunakan berasal dari periode Mei 2026. Pada tahap selanjutnya, InSet Lexicon-Based digunakan untuk melabeli data pelatihan dan data uji, sementara algoritma Naïve Bayes diterapkan sebagai model klasifikasi sentimen. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa model menghasilkan akurasi sebesar 88%. Pada kategori sentimen negatif, model memperoleh 0,86 untuk precision, 0,98 untuk recall, dan 0,90 untuk f1-score, menunjukkan kemampuan yang baik dalam mengenali ulasan negatif. Sebaliknya, kinerja untuk kategori positif cenderung lebih rendah. Berdasarkan hasil analisis, opini negatif mendominasi ulasan pengguna. Namun evaluasi dan perbaikan tetap diperlukan berdasarkan keluhan pengguna guna meningkatkan kualitas serta layanan dan pengembangan aplikasi di masa depan.

title: QUANTUM FEATURE ENCODING FOR ENHANCING CNN-BASED IMAGE CLASSIFICATION PERFORMANCE
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have exposed robust results for classifying images in data analytics. On the other hand, the effectiveness of these models is often limited by their substantial computational complexities, particularly when dealing with features represented in complex mathematical environments, multi class image classification, and especially when dealing with complex nonlinear relationships between features, which need to be addressed for transparent decision-making processes. This study developed a Quantum-Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network (Q-CNN) model, which incorporates traditional convolution-based feature extraction, Quantum Feature Encoding, and quantum processing. The developed model applies a quantum encoding mechanism to map classical features to quantum states for alternative feature representations and classification purposes. Experimental results show that the Q-CNN outperformed the standard CNN, reaching 97% training and validation accuracy compared to 94%, and lowering training and validation losses from 17% and 18% to 9% and 11%, respectively. Furthermore, precision, recall, and F1-score were increased from 90%, 88%, and 89% to 92%, 94%, and 93%, respectively. These findings demonstrate the potential effectiveness of quantum feature encoding for image classification tasks and provide a structured framework for enriched feature representation in convolution-based image processing models.

title: Novel Aspects of Ant Colony Optimization and Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: A Mobile Ad Hoc Network (MANET) is a collection of mobile nodes dynamically organized such that the connections among them frequently change. For carrying out conversation inside the system, routing algorithm is utilized to find path among nodes. The main objective of this type of ad-hoc system routing algorithm is accurate and competent path creation among a couple of nodes. This way, information would be conveyed in an appropriate way. Path building ought to be carried out with a least amount of bandwidth utilization and overheads. A wireless ad-hoc system is a structure installed exclusive of some infrastructure. Topics comprise of learning on routing algorithms for advanced efficiency, and practical concerns in its application. These areas are critical to construct a support in design, execution, operation, and examination of wireless ad-hoc system. This chapter will highlight mainly essential features of eminent algorithms particle swarm optimization (PSO) and Ant colony optimization (ACO). It deals with hybridization of two algorithms ACO and PSO. Merging the strengths of two algorithms will solve complex problems in various fields.

title: Optimizing Curriculum Design with Fuzzy Logic in Computational Intelligence
abstract: The purpose of this work is to investigate the optimization of class design through the utilization of fuzzy sense within the field of computational intelligence, pulling perceptivity from educational exploration. When it comes to meeting the diverse and ever-changing needs of students, traditional classroom layouts frequently struggle to adequately accommodate them. A good outcome can be achieved by the utilization of fuzzy sense, which can deal with queries and nebulosity. The purpose of this project is to investigate how fuzzy sense can be utilized to develop educational programs that are more flexible and individualized. The approach that has been described enables nuanced decision-making in the context of classroom development. This is accomplished by incorporating both expert knowledge and feedback from students into fuzzy conclusion systems. A comparative review of several models reveals that fuzzy sense is beneficial in improving the inflexibility of the classroom and the responsiveness to the needs of the students. Case studies derived from diverse educational environments exhibit realistic implementations and benefits, such as improved student engagement and literacy concerns. In light of the findings, it appears that the fuzzy sense-grounded class design not only caters to the preferences of individual students in terms of literacy but also improves the quality of education as a whole. This exploration contributes to the current efforts to facilitate the implementation of educational methods through the use of computational intelligence.

title: NBS: No Bias Stereo
abstract: Stereo reconstruction is one of the last remaining Computer Vision tasks where all state-of-the-art methods employ a heavy architectural inductive bias. Even though it has been demonstrated that the task can be solved using general-purpose methods, it is widely believed that inductive biases in stereo are strictly necessary for both high-quality results and computational efficiency. We challenge this paradigm. In this paper, we demonstrate that both state-of-the-art accuracy and superior runtime efficiency are achievable with a model completely devoid of architectural inductive biases, relying instead on a simple, end-to-end Vision Transformer. By training on massive synthetic datasets, we show that pure data-driven learning can surpass explicitly engineered geometry. This work proves that explicit inductive biases are no longer a prerequisite for stereo matching, ultimately unlocking true scaling laws for continuous improvement in 3D reconstruction.

title: How Proper Scoring Rules Shape LLM Forecasting
abstract: This paper evaluates how reward function choice shapes the performance and behavior of LLM forecasters. We compare five proper scoring rules as training objectives for binary forecasts of resolved real-world events. Although the rules share the same theoretical incentive for truthful probability reporting, the resulting models differ in calibration, probability use, and estimated profiles of bias, information, and noise, with smaller differences in aggregate accuracy and discrimination. The Brier-trained model has the lowest observed Brier score and highest AUC-ROC, while the log-trained model has the highest observed log score and lowest calibration error. Models with similar aggregate performance also reach that performance through different combinations of bias, information, and noise. Proper scoring rules therefore need not behave interchangeably as training objectives. Reward choice may shape not only how well an LLM forecasts, but how its forecasting errors are structured.
